music_content_accompany_332_about: The right hand runs down the chord in groups of three, three and two. The root lands with each group.
music_content_accompany_alberti_about: Low, high, middle, high in the left hand, the right hand's chord on 1 and 3.
music_content_accompany_ballad_about: The left hand climbs root, fifth, octave and tenth twice a bar under a held right-hand chord.
music_content_accompany_block_13_about: The root and the chord together on beats 1 and 3.
music_content_accompany_block_1_about: Both hands strike the chord on beat 1 and hold the bar: the root below, the chord above.
music_content_accompany_boogie_about: Eight to the bar, up the chord and back (1 3 5 6 b7 6 5 3) and swung, with right-hand chords on 2 and 4.
music_content_accompany_broken_about: The right hand rocks up and down the chord in eighths over a held root.
music_content_accompany_chart_1_about: Eight bars of triads, one a bar, closing on V and I.
music_content_accompany_chart_2_about: Sevenths join the triads, and some bars change chord on beat 3.
music_content_accompany_chart_2_label: Chart 2: two chords in some bars
music_content_accompany_chart_3_about: Sus and add9 colours and slash chords (the bass named after the slash).
music_content_accompany_chart_3_label: Chart 3: sus, add9 and slash bass
music_content_accompany_comp_and24_about: Red Garland's offbeats: the and of 2, then the next chord early on the and of 4.
music_content_accompany_comp_and2_4_abou: Short stabs on the and of 2 and on 4, room for a line on top.
music_content_accompany_comp_bossa_about: On 1, the and of 2 and 4, straight eighths.
music_content_accompany_comp_hardbop_abo: Short hits with the drummer: on 1, the and of 2, then the next chord pushed on the and of 4.
music_content_accompany_comp_waltz1_abou: Jazz waltz comping in 3/4: on 1, then the and of 2.
music_content_accompany_comp_waltz2_abou: In 3/4, leave 1 to the bass and comp on 2 and 3.
music_content_accompany_comp_whole_about: One chord a bar, on 1, held.
music_content_accompany_gospel_about: The chord, its IV over the same bass on the and of 2, and back on 4: the gospel and rock 1-4-1.
music_content_accompany_half_time_about: Root and chord on 1, then the next bar's chord pushed early on the and of 4.
music_content_accompany_lead_1_about: Quarters and eighths, chord tones on 1 and 3, played swung.
music_content_accompany_lead_2_about: Eighth-note lines and anticipations: the and of 4 tied into the next chord.
music_content_accompany_left_rootless_ab: Rootless A or B (3 5 7 9 or 7 9 3 5) on each chord and each bar line, whichever moves least.
music_content_accompany_left_roots_about: The root on each chord and each bar line.
music_content_accompany_left_shells_abou: Root and 7th (root and 5th on a triad) on each chord and each bar line.
music_content_accompany_lh_137_about: Left hand: root, 3rd, 7th (the 5th on a triad).
music_content_accompany_lh_173_about: Left hand: root, 7th, then the 3rd on top.
music_content_accompany_lh_alt_about: Left hand: 1-3-7 or 1-7-3, whichever moves least from the chord before.
music_content_accompany_lh_octave_about: Left hand: the root in octaves, short, with the right hand (Horace Silver's punches). Right hand: rootless A or B.
music_content_accompany_lh_root_then_abo: Left hand: the root. Right hand: rootless A or B.
music_content_accompany_lh_rootless_abou: Left hand: 3 5 7 9 or 7 9 3 5 (3 13 7 9 or 7 9 3 13 on a dominant), whichever moves least. The bass player has the root.
music_content_accompany_lh_two_feel_abou: Left hand: root on 1, fifth on 3. Right hand: the 3rd and 7th on the rhythm.
music_content_accompany_pop_sync_about: Both hands together on 1, the and of 2, and 4.
music_content_accompany_r58_about: The left hand walks root, fifth, octave, fifth in quarters under a held right-hand chord.
music_content_accompany_rock_about: Left-hand octaves on every eighth, the right hand's chord on 1 and 3.
music_content_accompany_shuffle_about: The rock and roll left hand: root and fifth, root and sixth, in swung eighths.
music_content_accompany_spread_about: The left hand opens root, fifth, tenth, fifth in quarters under a held right-hand chord.
music_content_accompany_stride_about: Left hand only: the root in octaves on 1, the chord on 2, a tenth on 3, the chord on 4.
music_content_accompany_stride_lite_abou: Left hand only: the root on 1, the chord on 2, the fifth on 3, the chord on 4.
music_content_accompany_under_melody_abo: The left hand on roots. On each chord change the right hand adds the chord below the melody note.
music_content_analysis_rule_backdoor: A backdoor: bVII7 going up a step to I. The iv7 before it pairs with it.
music_content_analysis_rule_dominant: The V: a dominant that resolves down a fifth to the key's I, or a ii-V left hanging. A hanging ii-V names the key a fifth below.
music_content_analysis_rule_ii: The ii of a ii-V: a minor (or half-diminished) chord a fourth below the V.
music_content_analysis_rule_other: Not part of a cadence. It's named in the last key reached, or in the next key when it's none of the last key's chords. iv and bVI count as borrowed from the minor.
music_content_analysis_rule_passing_dim: A passing diminished 7th: it links two chords a step apart.
music_content_analysis_rule_related_ii: A related ii: the ii before a secondary dominant or a tritone sub.
music_content_analysis_rule_secondary: A secondary dominant: it resolves down a fifth to a chord that isn't a key's I. It belongs to that chord's key.
music_content_analysis_rule_tonic: A key's I: the home chord, or a major chord reached from its own V7, tritone sub or backdoor. A minor i needs its whole iiø7 V7 and two bars.
music_content_analysis_rule_tritone_sub: A tritone sub: a dominant that resolves down a half step, in place of the V a tritone away.
music_content_catalog_accompany_blurb: Play pop, blues and gospel patterns, jazz comping or a lead sheet over a chord chart in any key.
music_content_catalog_aerophone_blurb: Learn the fingerings in Roland's lesson order, then hold, swell and tongue notes and land intervals against a drone.
music_content_catalog_by_ear_blurb: Loop a part of a recording you own, slow it down, mark its sections and play it back, or find its tonic.
music_content_catalog_call_response_blur: Hear a short call over a groove and play it back in time, or answer it with your own phrase that lands on a chord tone.
music_content_catalog_chord_scales_blurb: As a ii-V-I moves, play the go-to scale for each chord.
music_content_catalog_chords_blurb: Fret an open chord string by string, strum it, or change between two chords in time.
music_content_catalog_circle_blurb: Key signatures, the order of sharps and flats, neighbours and each key's chords, fast.
music_content_catalog_comping_blurb: Play a blues phrase in the right hand over a Charleston shell in the left.
music_content_catalog_ear_bass_lines_blu: Hear chords from I and write down the bass line by degree.
music_content_catalog_ear_cadences_blurb: Hear two chords that end a phrase and name the cadence.
music_content_catalog_ear_chord_function: Hear a chord after the key is set and name its place in the key, I to vii°.
music_content_catalog_ear_chord_qualitie: Hear a chord and say whether it is major, minor or another quality.
music_content_catalog_ear_fine_pitch_blu: Hear whether a note is a few cents sharp or flat of another.
music_content_catalog_ear_interval_compa: Hear two intervals and say which one is bigger.
music_content_catalog_ear_intervals_blur: Hear two notes and name the distance between them.
music_content_catalog_ear_inversions_blu: Hear a chord and say which of its notes is in the bass.
music_content_catalog_ear_melody_dictati: Hear a three or four note phrase and play it back in order.
music_content_catalog_ear_mixed_blurb: A short mix of the nine ear drills that adapts to you. Pick which go in.
music_content_catalog_ear_progressions_b: Hear three or four chords starting on I and write down the rest, or hear where a key change goes.
music_content_catalog_ear_repertoire_tra: Hear a short phrase from one of your saved songs and play it back.
music_content_catalog_ear_scale_degrees_: Hear the tonic, then a note, and name its place in the key.
music_content_catalog_ear_scales_blurb: Hear a scale over its tonic and name it, from major and minor to the modes.
music_content_catalog_ear_song_loops_blu: Hear a song's chord loop as a groove after the key is set and name every chord.
music_content_catalog_ear_wrong_note_blu: Follow a written melody by ear and find the note that was played wrong.
music_content_catalog_feel_blurb: Hear a groove and say whether it is straight, swung, a shuffle or in 12/8.
music_content_catalog_fretboard_blurb: Work finger patterns, box shapes, note names and intervals on the neck.
music_content_catalog_jam_blurb: Solo over a progression with the chord tones lit for each chord.
music_content_catalog_lab_blurb: Play freely and record everything, with or without a backing track.
music_content_catalog_licks_blurb: Hear a transcribed line over the changes, then play it back.
music_content_catalog_listening_blurb: Hear a loop flat and changed, and name the change: an EQ band, a level, a pan, compression or a delay.
music_content_catalog_pads_blurb: Finger-drumming technique, a repertoire of grooves in six levels, and holding the tempo without a click.
music_content_catalog_pedal_blurb: Legato pedalling: lift the sustain pedal just after each chord and press it straight back.
music_content_catalog_phrases_blurb: Popular short phrases for your instrument: famous public-domain tunes and a style's stock licks, heard and played back.
music_content_catalog_reading_blurb: Read notes on the staff and name or play them, or play a short generated phrase.
music_content_catalog_rhythm_blurb: Tap a steady pulse, read a pattern and tap it, or hear one and tap or write it back.
music_content_catalog_scales_blurb: Play a scale, an arpeggio or a broken chord evenly at the target tempo, in any key.
music_content_catalog_song_blurb: Play through one of your saved songs while Woodshed waits for you or keeps time.
music_content_catalog_strum_blurb: Strum a known chord progression in time while the microphone follows along.
music_content_catalog_two_hand_blurb: Each hand plays its own part: a steady pulse under a moving line, or both hands mirroring.
music_content_catalog_voicings_blurb: Play rootless jazz voicings through a ii-V-I in all twelve keys.
music_content_circle_ask_across: Across the circle from {key}? (Its dominant is the tritone substitute.)
music_content_circle_ask_borrowed: {shown}. Which chord is borrowed from {key} minor?
music_content_circle_ask_count_major: How many sharps or flats in {key} major?
music_content_circle_ask_count_minor: How many sharps or flats in {key} minor?
music_content_circle_ask_major_none: Which major key has no sharps or flats?
music_content_circle_ask_minor_none: Which minor key has no sharps or flats?
music_content_circle_ask_secondary: {shown}. Which chord is a secondary dominant (a V of another chord)?
music_content_circle_ask_signature_major: Which major key is this signature?
music_content_circle_ask_signature_minor: Which minor key is this signature?
music_content_circle_ask_v_of: {shown}. {chord} is the V of which chord?
music_content_ear_bass_lines_description: Chords from I: write down the bass, degree by degree.
music_content_ear_chord_functions_descri: I, IV, V, I sets the key, then one chord plays. Which is it, I to vii°?
music_content_ear_data_drill_cadences_de: Name the cadence in a given key: authentic, plagal, half or deceptive.
music_content_ear_data_drill_chord_quali: Name triads and seventh chords by ear.
music_content_ear_data_drill_intervals_d: Hear two notes and name the distance: ascending, descending or harmonic.
music_content_ear_data_drill_melody_dict: Hear a short phrase and play it back in order.
music_content_ear_data_drill_mixed_descr: A short adaptive mix of the nine ear drills. Pick which ones go in.
music_content_ear_data_drill_repertoire_: Phrases from your saved songs, mapped back to scale degrees.
music_content_ear_data_drill_scale_degre: Hear a note over the tonic and name its scale degree.
music_content_ear_fine_pitch_description: Two notes a few cents apart: is the second higher or lower?
music_content_ear_interval_compare_descr: Two intervals, one after the other: which is bigger?
music_content_ear_inversions_description: A chord with its root, third, fifth or seventh in the bass: which inversion?
music_content_ear_level_anchor_summary: Hear the tonic and the dominant: 1 and 5.
music_content_ear_level_chromatic_summar: Add the colour tones b2 and #4 to the seven diatonic degrees.
music_content_ear_level_full_summary: Review every scale degree Woodshed teaches so far.
music_content_ear_level_major_pentachord: Map the first five major degrees around the tonic.
music_content_ear_level_minor_diatonic_s: Recognise natural-minor functions around the tonic.
music_content_ear_progressions_descripti: Three or four chords starting on I: write down the rest. Or a key change: where it goes, and how.
music_content_ear_scales_description: A scale over its tonic: major, the minors, pentatonics, blues and the modes.
music_content_ear_song_loops_description: The key is set, then a chord loop plays as a groove: name every chord.
music_content_ear_wrong_note_description: A written melody plays with one note changed: which one?
music_content_loops_borrowed_hint: iv, bVI, bVII and bIII beside I, IV, V and vi.
music_content_loops_minor_hint: i, iv, v and V, with bVI, bIII and bVII from the natural minor.
music_content_loops_modal_hint: Dorian, Mixolydian, Lydian, Phrygian and Aeolian.
music_content_loops_pop_hint: I, IV, V and vi in the four loops pop is made of.
music_content_loops_rock_hint: bVII, bVI and bIII: the rock and Mixolydian loops.
music_content_loops_songs_hint: Real songs' chords, in a key you hear first.
music_content_loops_tritone_hint: bII7 to I against V7 to I.
music_content_tunes_jazz_blues_composer: Traditional form (Bags' Groove, Now's the Time)
music_content_tunes_reharm_backdoor_abou: Reach the next chord from iv7 to bVII7 (Fm7 Bb7 to C).
music_content_tunes_reharm_chromatic_abo: Its second half becomes the ii-V a half step above the next chord (Ebm7 Ab7 to Dm7).
music_content_tunes_reharm_passing_dim_a: Its second half becomes a diminished 7th a half step below the next chord.
music_content_tunes_reharm_related_ii_ab: A dominant shares its time with its ii (G7 becomes Dm7 G7).
music_content_tunes_reharm_secondary_abo: The chord becomes the dominant of the chord after it (Am7 before Dm7 becomes A7).
music_content_tunes_reharm_tritone_about: A dominant becomes the dominant a tritone away (G7 to Db7).
music_content_tunes_rhythm_changes_compo: After George Gershwin's I Got Rhythm (Oleo, Anthropology)
